# Berlin One-Year Lease Review Checklist

A one-year apartment lease in Berlin should be checked for rent details, termination rules, deposit terms, and what is included in the monthly payment. For your case, the key numbers are **EUR 1,450/month rent**, **EUR 3,000 deposit**, and **move-in on 2026-06-01**.

## Lease Clauses to Review Before Signing

| Area | What to check | Why it matters |
|---|---|---|
| Lease term | Fixed end date, renewal rules, early termination rights | A one-year lease can be hard to exit early |
| Rent type | Warmmiete vs Kaltmiete; what is included | Determines your real monthly cost |
| Deposit | Amount, where it is held, repayment timeline | Protects your cash and return rights |
| Utilities | Heating, water, electricity, internet, waste, building services | Avoid surprise bills |
| Indexation / increase | Any rent increase clause, escalation, or inflation link | Prevents unexpected higher rent |
| Subletting | Whether subletting is allowed and under what conditions | Important if plans change |
| Repairs | Who pays for which repairs, minor damage, maintenance | Avoid unfair cost shifting |
| Handover condition | Written inventory, condition report, keys, meters | Essential for deposit protection |
| Notice and termination | Notice period, special termination rights, landlord rights | Controls how and when the lease ends |
| House rules | Noise, pets, smoking, use of common areas | Can affect daily living and compliance |

## Questions to Ask the Landlord

- Is **EUR 1,450** the total **warm rent**, or is it only base rent?
- Which costs are included: **heating, water, garbage, building cleaning, internet, electricity**?
- How is the **EUR 3,000 deposit** held, and will it be placed in a separate tenant deposit account?
- Is the apartment **furnished or unfurnished**, and what items are included in writing?
- Are **pets**, **subletting**, or **home office use** allowed?
- What is the **notice period** if I need to leave early?
- Are there any planned **renovations, construction, or building issues**?
- Will I receive a **signed handover protocol** with meter readings and photos?
- Who is responsible for **minor repairs** and what is the repair limit?
- When will I receive the **final utility settlement** after move-out?

## Costs That Are Commonly Extra in Berlin

| Cost item | Often paid separately? | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| Electricity | Yes | Usually separate from rent |
| Internet / TV | Yes | Check if building has a provider restriction |
| Tenant liability insurance | Usually yes | Strongly recommended |
| GEZ / broadcasting contribution | Yes, if applicable | Paid per household, not per person |
| Heating / hot water | Sometimes included | Depends on warm rent setup |
| Gas | Sometimes separate | Less common in fully managed apartments |
| Move-in service / elevator booking | Sometimes | Common in larger buildings |
| Furniture / kitchen use fees | Sometimes | Only if explicitly listed |
| Final cleaning | Sometimes disputed | Avoid unclear clauses; document condition well |

## Move-In and Move-Out Documentation

### At Move-In
- Take **date-stamped photos and video** of every room, floor, walls, windows, radiators, bathroom, kitchen, appliances, and balcony if any.
- Record **meter readings** for electricity, water, gas, and heating if accessible.
- Check and list **all keys**: apartment, building, mailbox, cellar, bike room, garage.
- Create a **signed handover protocol** with the landlord or agent.
- Note every defect: scratches, stains, broken fixtures, missing items, and existing wear.
- Save copies of the **lease, inventory list, handover protocol, and all messages**.

### At Move-Out
- Clean the apartment to the standard required in the lease.
- Repeat **photos/video** in the same rooms and lighting if possible.
- Record **final meter readings** and take photos of the meters.
- Return **all keys** and get written confirmation of the return.
- Ask for a **move-out protocol** signed by both sides.
- Keep proof of the forwarding address for deposit return and utility settlement.

## Clauses That Need Extra Attention

- **Fixed-term justification**: In Germany, a fixed-term lease usually needs a valid reason stated in the contract. Check that the reason is clearly written.
- **Deposit deductions**: The lease should not allow vague deductions without proof.
- **Minor repair clauses**: These should have a clear cap and apply only to small everyday repairs.
- **Renovation obligations**: Be careful with any clause that forces you to repaint or renovate regardless of condition.
- **Visit / access rights**: The landlord should not have unlimited access without notice.
- **Furniture and fixtures**: If anything is included, it should be listed specifically.
- **German-language control**: If you sign a bilingual lease, check which version controls in case of conflict.

## Quick Actions
